question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Lineage-resolved heritability of AP-1 activity
ideas.description: Barcode single cells (LARRY/Watermelon-style) and profile sister and cousin cells by scRNA-seq or live AP-1 reporter imaging to compute how AP-1 activity autocorrelates across divisions. Comparing the decay constant for AP-1 target output against other signaling-responsive programs gives a quantitative, assumption-light test of whether AP-1 state is actually heritable rather than just stimulus-driven.

ideas.title: Degron separation of establishment from maintenance
ideas.description: Tag FOS/JUN with a degron and deplete AP-1 either before stimulation or hours after the state has formed, then read out accessibility (ATAC) and restimulation response. True memory predicts that the primed state persists after AP-1 protein is removed, whereas a purely sustained-signal model predicts collapse.

ideas.title: Prime-rest-rechallenge transcriptional priming assay
ideas.description: Deliver a defined transient stimulus, wash out and rest cells for varying intervals and division numbers, then rechallenge and measure the amplitude and latency of AP-1 target induction by nascent RNA (TT-seq or single-molecule FISH). Faster or larger secondary responses that decay with time and divisions directly quantify the strength and lifetime of the memory.

ideas.title: Synthetic AP-1 site array for sufficiency
ideas.description: Integrate arrays of AP-1 motifs (and motif-scrambled controls) at a neutral genomic locus adjacent to a reporter, then drive AP-1 binding transiently with an optogenetic or chemically inducible Fos/Jun module. Persistent reporter expression and accessibility after induction ends would show AP-1 binding is sufficient to write a heritable state, independent of pre-existing locus context.

ideas.title: Does the memory survive replication and mitosis?
ideas.description: Compare persistence of AP-1-primed accessibility in cycling cells versus cells arrested pharmacologically or in post-mitotic states, and perform mitotic-chromosome CUT&RUN to test for AP-1 bookmarking. This distinguishes a slowly-decaying protein/chromatin state from a genuinely replication-heritable epigenetic mechanism and identifies the step where memory is copied or lost.

candidates: Clonal barcoding (e.g. Watermelon/LARRY) plus scRNA-seq to ask whether AP-1 activity level is heritable across sister and cousin cells
Live-cell FOS/JUN reporter imaging across lineages to measure autocorrelation time of AP-1 activity and how it decays with each division
Pulse-chase ATAC-seq after transient stimulation to test whether AP-1-bound enhancers stay open long after AP-1 protein is gone
Acute degron depletion of FOS/JUN before vs after stimulus to separate establishment from maintenance of the accessible state
Dose-response priming: give stimulus once, wait, restimulate, and measure whether response amplitude/speed is enhanced at AP-1 sites (transcriptional priming assay)
Single-molecule tracking of JUN to compare residence times at primed vs naive enhancers
CUT&RUN time course of AP-1 plus partner TFs to see whether AP-1 departure precedes or follows loss of the memory state
Mitotic bookmarking test: fixed-cell imaging and mitotic CUT&RUN to ask whether AP-1 stays chromatin-bound through mitosis
Synthetic AP-1 site array integrated at a neutral locus to test whether AP-1 binding alone is sufficient to create a heritable open state
Optogenetic or chemogenetic pulsatile AP-1 induction to map the stimulus duration/amplitude threshold required for persistent state change
Hi-C/Micro-C before and after transient AP-1 induction to test whether memory is stored as persistent enhancer-promoter loops
Measure partner-dependence: knock out individual Jun/Fos family members and see which are required for maintenance vs induction
Test chromatin remodeler dependence (BRG1/SMARCA4, p300) in maintaining AP-1-primed accessibility after AP-1 removal
DNA methylation and H3K4me1 profiling at AP-1 sites to see whether a covalent mark accompanies the persistent state
Replication-coupled assay: block cell cycle vs allow division to ask whether memory survives DNA replication
Mathematical modeling and fitting of AP-1 autoregulatory feedback (JUN autoactivation) to test bistability predictions
Perturb-seq with AP-1 family and cofactor sgRNAs read out by a memory reporter to find the maintenance machinery
Cross-stimulus generalization test: prime with one signal, challenge with a different AP-1-engaging signal, measure transfer of memory
Compare AP-1 memory across cell types and in post-mitotic vs dividing cells to test division dependence
In vivo lineage tracing of AP-1-high cells (FOS-CreER) to test whether past AP-1 activity predicts future cell fate or drug tolerance
